paper.title: Buffer of Thoughts: Thought-Augmented Reasoning with Large Language Models
paper.central_claim: BoT dynamically distills and retains high-level thought-templates from solved problems, retrieves and instantiates them for later tasks, and continually improves reasoning accuracy, efficiency, generalization and robustness through a buffer-manager.

notes: actual_model supplied by invocation environment; no independent routing probe performed.
No seat-specific session identifier or receipt exposed to this worker. Historical outcome sections of required pattern assets are not used as evidence or scoring inputs.

sections_read: Complete supplied text lines 1–2542: abstract, §§1–8, Table 1 and all figure captions, references, Appendix A.1 six templates and A.2–A.3 prompts

evidence.quote: If we initialize an empty meta-buffer or encounter a problem without a proper thought-template, the distilled thought-templates will be directly stored in the meta-buffer.
evidence.support_explanation: Unmatched solutions become persistent templates without an explicit correctness gate.
Admission uses embedding novelty, not measured marginal utility.

evidence.quote: In this ablation study, we divide the entire process into four rounds. In each round, we randomly sample 50 questions from each benchmark and conduct reasoning. In the subsequent round, we continue to randomly sample another 50 questions from each benchmark.
evidence.support_explanation: Later rounds use earlier retained templates; distinctness/deduplication across rounds is not explicitly guaranteed.

evidence.quote: In contrast, the model without the buffer-manager fails to exhibit an upward trend.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-reported manager-off comparison; curve values are not in the fixed text.

evidence.quote: BoT requires only 12% of the cost of multi-query methods
evidence.support_explanation: Relative inference cost claim, not a full construction/maintenance ledger.

evidence.quote: this evaluation process 10 times and take the average accuracy as the success rate of different methods on each benchmark.
evidence.support_explanation: Repeated evaluation average is reported, but not cross-buffer/search variance or intervals.

evidence.quote: We randomly sample 1000 examples from various benchmarks as a test subset and evaluate different methods on this subset.
evidence.support_explanation: Sample size for robustness evaluation, not all main benchmark denominators.

evidence.quote: In contrast, our BoT directly retrieves a thought-template in code format, thus a program is instantiated to traverse combinations of numbers and symbols, thereby eliminating the need to build the reasoning structure from scratch.
evidence.support_explanation: Program execution/enumeration is a substantive alternative explanation to abstract thought alone.

evidence.quote: we choose six different benchmarks, each sampled with 100 distinct tasks. We update the meta-buffer from scratch, and after completing all sampled tasks, we display the number of derived thought-templates.
evidence.support_explanation: Buffer-building procedure and denominators, not frozen unseen-category evaluation.

signatures.object: Persistent meta-buffer of task-description, solution-description and high-level thought-template triples
signatures.information: Distilled input plus past generated solution steps/code; embedding similarity of task descriptions
signatures.operation: Distill reusable template, append if new, retrieve maximum-similarity template and instantiate; use three coarse fallback templates when unmatched
signatures.conditions: Recurring task structure, capable initializer, embedding similarity threshold δ approximately 0.5–0.7
signatures.feedback: Observed problem-solving trajectories; correctness verification before admission is not specified
signatures.selection_rule: Empty/unmatched buffer: direct insertion; otherwise insert only if maximum embedding similarity < δ
signatures.selection_data: Online problem stream, with task-family templates and fixed exemplars
signatures.persistence: Meta-buffer grows across problems and rounds; no explicit rollback/deletion policy
signatures.later_use: Retrieve templates from previously solved tasks for subsequent sampled questions
signatures.claimed_effect: Higher accuracy, lower inference time, stability and continual growth
signatures.failure_boundary: Bad initial templates, semantic similarity not utility, weak creativity gains and uncertain cross-round overlap

gap.author_gap: Single-query prompting lacks reusable high-level structure; multi-query searches rebuild reasoning expensively.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete residual is reuse of parameterized reasoning structures rather than repeated per-query search or raw examples.

lineage.source: Fixed BoT v2 §§1–2, Table 1; cited originals not supplied

gap.closest_adjacent: Meta-Prompting and PAL already offer expert decomposition or executable reasoning; Table 1 compares them, but not a matched retrieval-of-raw-examples or fixed-template alternative.
gap.residue: Whether abstraction itself, rather than solver code or extra calls, produces the gain remains incompletely isolated.
gap.stakes: Amortizing reasoning across recurring tasks can reduce repeated inference work.
gap.remaining_gap: No independently grounded retention-quality gate or clean frozen construction/evaluation split, and cost lacks complete amortization accounting.

claims.text: BoT improves reasoning across ten tasks
claims.baseline_control: Standard, CoT, ExpertPrompting, PAL, ToT, GoT, Meta-Prompting; distiller/buffer removal
claims.selection_vs_test: Online buffer construction/evaluation separation insufficiently described
claims.result_denominator: Table 1 BoT Game24 82.4 vs ToT 74.0; shapes 93.6 vs MetaPrompting 78.2; checkmate 86.4 vs 57.2; main n not uniformly supplied
claims.counterevidence: No category holdout or complete matched alternative; exact figure ablation magnitudes unavailable in supplied text.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported benchmark point-estimate superiority for the full recipe.

claims.setting: Four rounds, 50 sampled questions per task per round; GPT-4 and Llama3-70B
claims.selection_vs_test: Earlier templates reused later; random resampling overlap not explicitly excluded
claims.result_denominator: Qualitative upward trajectory versus no upward trend, Figure 9 caption/text only
claims.counterevidence: No isolated utility gate, stream-order variance, or numerical trajectory in text.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Limited author-reported subsequent-task retained benefit, not indefinite monotonic improvement.

claims.text: Only 12% multi-query cost and stronger robustness
claims.setting: Ten tasks for cost; sampled 1000-item subset repeated ten evaluations for robustness
claims.result_denominator: 12% average relative inference cost; robustness repeated means without reported intervals
claims.counterevidence: Full wall-clock/token ledger and repeated-buffer uncertainty absent.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Reported inference-time savings in these settings, not end-to-end lifecycle savings.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author reports growing templates helping subsequent sampled tasks across four rounds with manager-off contrast; main benchmark and inference-cost gains apply to the complete BoT recipe. No improver improvement, verified monotonic growth or clean unseen-category transfer is demonstrated.
unresolved: Cross-round overlap and construction/test separation; unavailable figure values; full lifecycle cost.

reason: In-scope retained non-weight reasoning-template store; complete text supports scoped later-round reuse and benchmark gains, not guaranteed continual improvement.
